name: Extract evidence pieces and tag to policy queries

llm.prompt_template:
You are reading a document about a company or industry association's
engagement on climate policy. Extract every distinct PIECE of evidence
that takes a position (explicit or implicit) on one of the policy
queries below. Skip purely descriptive or operational content.

Policy queries (return query_id):
  Q1  climate_science          — alignment with IPCC science
  Q2  energy_transition        — speed and direction of energy transition
  Q3  ghg_emissions            — emissions accounting & reduction
  Q4  energy_disclosure        — disclosure of climate risks/positions
  Q5  carbon_tax_pricing
  Q6  emissions_trading
  Q7  renewable_energy_policy
  Q8  energy_efficiency_policy
  Q9  fossil_fuel_subsidies
  Q10 transport_policy
  Q11 industry_specific_policy
  Q12 climate_lobbying_disclosure
  Q13 climate_lobbying_governance

Document (entity_id={entity_id}, source_class={source_class},
published_at={published_at}):
---
{body}
---

Return a JSON list, one object per evidence piece:
  [{{"query_id": "Q3", "quote": "...verbatim from text...",
     "stance_summary": "supports / opposes / mixed / unclear",
     "confidence": 0.0-1.0,
     "char_offset_start": int, "char_offset_end": int}},
   ...]

Empty list if no policy-relevant evidence found.

review.rationale:
Low-confidence extractions propagate downstream into scoring; even a
light human pass on the low-confidence subset materially improves
cell-aggregation quality.

compiler_notes: Methodology references 14 queries (line 254) but Table 4 enumerates 13. Treating Table 4 as canonical.

Char offsets are nullable because some upstream document formats (PDFs with OCR, scraped HTML) don't preserve clean offsets. Real production pipeline should improve upstream parsing rather than work around here.

eval.notes:
Eval pattern: hand-label a small set of documents with their expected
(query_id, quote) pairs. The metric isn't exact-match — it's whether
the LLM finds the same set of policy-relevant pieces a human would.
